- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.11) and forecast spikes, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.06) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 2–5% to reflect sentiment-driven correction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, cap forecast peak at 1–2% below recent high to prevent mean reversion miss.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.22 or lower), apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence in short-term rallies.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by 2–3% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to reflect mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.06–0.11), forecast should not exceed 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid lagged overreaction.
